To redeem the 15% off on Guest Rooms, Aesthetic Spa services, and dining in Babbo, the following conditions apply:

  • Physical Season Pass Required: Guests must present their physical 2025–2026 Hockley Valley Resort season pass upon Hotel check-in, arrival at Spa appointment and dining in Babbo (alcohol not included) prior to ordering. No photos or photocopies.

  • Hotel Room Discount Conditions: Valid only on regular-priced or Bed & Breakfast package room rates. Reservations must be booked directly through Hockley Valley Resort and are not valid through third-party booking agents.
  • Seasonal Validity: Discount is valid only during the active 2025–2026 ski season and cannot be carried over or deferred.

Winter 2025-2026 Ski Race Program

Join our Winter 2025-2026 Ski Race Program, designed to build a strong foundation for young skiers’ athletic development across physical, technical, tactical, and mental domains. We emphasize a safe and supportive learning environment where guided self-discovery, encouragement, and enthusiasm flourish.

Program Highlights:

Vision: To provide a solid foundation and knowledge base to enhance skiers’ physical, technical, tactical, and mental abilities.

Core Values: Safe learning environment, guided self-discovery, friendliness, encouragement, support, enthusiasm, and thorough preparation.

Skill Requirements: Participants must be confident parallel skiers capable of skiing most of the time on intermediate and expert runs, including Face (Black), J.P. (Black), Boomerang (Blue), Slalom (Blue), Roller Coaster (Black), and Far Side (Black).

*Plus HST

FAQ

Can lift tickets be purchased by in-house guests on site if decided last minute?

If there is availability, yes. Guests can go to the Activity Centre counter if the counter in the ski café is not open.

Are lift tickets only available to purchase online?

All lift tickets and rentals should be booked online in advance to secure your booking.

IF you are booking lessons in person day of, refrain from booking lessons online ahead of time to avoid potential unavailability.

I purchased lift tickets online, where do I pick them up?

Lift ticket pick up is done at the counters of the Activity Centre and the ski café pro shop counter when open.

When buying the pack of eight lift tickets, it says it has to be assigned to a certain name. What if we want to split up the pack to different people?

Tickets for the voucher booklet: they are all transferable. Please give the ski department a call for more information. 519-942-0951 Option #5

What is the locker rental fee?

Locker Rental Fees: 2023-24 winter season, $249 (plus HST and $20 lock deposit). We will give you a refund for this amount when you return your lock to the Ticket Office at the end of the season.

I do not need a rental package, can I rent individual items?

Yes, if you do not need a rental package, you can rent what you need in person the day of.

Boots: $25

Skis: $25

Helmet: $10

Poles: $10

Promos and Programs?

We have several promos and programs. Please call the ski department for more information. 519-942-0951 Option #5

More information on lessons?

Please get in contact with the ski department for more information. 519-942-0951 Option #5

When is snow shoeing open?

Snowshoeing is open and the trail is condition dependent.

If weather conditions allow and have been groomed trails will remain open. Rentals are first come first serve in person.  The trail is not available from 5-9pm.

All lift tickets and rentals must be pre-purchased online. Book your lift tickets and rentals and join us for fun on the slopes!

OUR MAGIC CARPET!

We were delighted to have our “magic carpet” up and running for the third season.

What’s a “magic carpet” you ask? Simply put a conveyor belt that allows our new or learning ski/boarders an easy way to get up the hill. Just step on the belt and up to go. No handles or seats required.
It is a great new addition to our learn to ski program.

Come and check it out!

TERRAIN PARKS!

RAIL

A metal bar, either rounded or with a small flat surface, which a skier or snowboarder can slide across (called “jibbing”). Rails are defined as anything too thin for a skier to place both skis on without turning. Many people confuse rails with wider surfaces with boxes, however these are not, and are just rails with a little UHMWPE on top.

Table Top

Similar to a box, but much wider. Commonly used by beginners who want to become comfortable with box type surfaces before moving on to real boxes. Table Tops are very wide and therefore allow a skier or snowboarder to slide across the surface and is difficult to fall on.

Trees

Used as natural surfaces and can be found either on or off the trails. Rails and boxes have many different shapes and sizes: straight, sloped, curved (often called a “Rainbow”), or kinked. Rails, especially rainbow, will also be seen curving over obstacles or vehicles.

Park Bench & Picnic Tables

Many jib features resemble outdoor items used when snowboarding in urban areas, such as stair handrails, benches, tables, etc.

Box

Similar to a rail, but wider with an ultra high molecular weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) surface. May or may not have metal edges.
